terms.workload: a stable named product job with an explicit capability contract
terms.backend: the inference location, runtime, or service
terms.model: an exact model identifier and immutable revision where available
terms.adapter: an optional connector between a workload contract and a backend or model
terms.selection: the backend and model assigned to a workload, environment, and hardware class

selectionRules.productBoundary: Product code targets named workload and capability contracts, not vendor or model SDK identity and not a universal lowest-common-denominator client.
selectionRules.explicitScope: Selections are explicit per workload, environment, and hardware class where needed.
selectionRules.immutableIdentity: Mutable aliases are not accepted selection identity.
selectionRules.fallbackBoundary: Any fallback requires explicit product policy, applicable privacy review, observable effective selection, and fail-closed boundaries; local-to-hosted transfer is never silent.
selectionRules.unsupportedCapability: An unsupported required capability fails planning or startup and never silently degrades.
selectionRules.unselectedFootprint: Unselected adapters, backends, and models contribute zero dependency, configuration, credential, workflow, download, runtime, persistent, or network footprint.
selectionRules.downloadBoundary: Large model weights are never downloaded automatically; explicit selection discloses disk, RAM, VRAM, and network estimates plus removal behavior.
selectionRules.discoveryBoundary: Discovery automation may nominate a candidate but never promotes or changes the accepted default.
selectionRules.promotionBoundary: Acceptance and default promotion are per workload and require owner review of representative workload and platform evidence.
selectionRules.heterogeneousSelections: Different workloads may retain different models and backends.
selectionRules.compatibilityBoundary: Provider or protocol compatibility is not capability conformance.

supportingSources.scope: provider registry and explicit provider-and-model identifiers
provider packages implementing a common model interface
model selection factors including modalities, function calling, speed, and cost

verifiedDiscoveryExamples.name: Muse Glimmer 30B
verifiedDiscoveryExamples.announcedFacts: Meta describes a 30-billion-parameter open-weight agentic model under Apache-2.0 with text and image input, tool-use claims, and quantized language-model weights under 20 GB. Meta names local or serving targets including llama.cpp, MLX, ExecuTorch, Ollama, and vLLM, while stating that several optimized integrations will arrive in the coming days.
verifiedDiscoveryExamples.acceptanceBoundary: Discovery and vendor claims do not establish acceptance or a default. Exact model-card, artifact, backend, platform, workload, privacy, license, performance, rollback, and removal evidence remains required.
